content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text resolves the Matthew 1:16 collision by checking whether any verse's own words state the contrary, rather than weighing the read-together chain by footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "none", "why": "The judge marks D1 vs C3 UNDERDETERMINED because neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary, which is precisely the retired stating-verse test instead of chain-against-chain footing."}
